text: 🚨 🔥 Apple's forensic team found OpenAI used its stolen schematics to train an AI agent The ex-Apple engineer at the center of the suit allegedly downloaded a confidential circuit schematic, ran it through an AI agent at OpenAI, and then told a colleague to…

🔧 Trainium3 and TPUs now match or beat Nvidia's GB300 on cost per token SemiAnalysis says InferenceX shows it, and Trainium's descriptor engines hit peak HBM bandwidth at small message sizes, which Nvidia GPUs can't.

🧮 OpenAI preprint says one tensor geometry result cracks four open problems The paper ties the asymptotic spectrum of tensors to lower bounds for matrix multiplication and the Fourier transform. It also covers integer multiplication on multi-tape Turing machines and the Erdős-Rado sunflower problem. It's a GitHub preprint, so nobody has refereed it yet. If the proofs hold, one lemma doing the work of four papers is the real story.

⚖️ New York's AG now has a dedicated AI cop, and it can fine up to $25,000 per violation Letitia James created the ASSET Unit to enforce the RAISE Act (Jan 1, 2027) and the chatbot law (June 1, 2027). Frontier developers must report critical safety incidents within 72 hours. The chatbot law targets flattery and bots posing as human, and nobody has defined where sycophancy starts yet. That fight starts in court.

🚨 Nvidia reportedly caps Chinese customers at 49% of a data center operator's business Tom's Hardware reports that the rule applies globally, and Nvidia hasn't confirmed it. • The limit is 49%, so at least 51% must be non-Chinese • Operators outside China…

🏗️ "Vibe architecting" is the new name for letting your coding agent pick your stack A new arXiv paper shows that changing only the prompt wording gave structurally different systems for the same task, and almost nobody reviews those choices as architecture.

🪤 Anthropic built Siren, a honeypot that tempts AI agents to escape their sandbox Wired reports the test drops agents into 26 sandboxes with deliberate egress holes and a juicy file of passwords just outside. Claude Mythos 5 took the bait 25.8% of the time…

🧹 Phil Schmid deleted most of his agent rules for Gemini 4 Neon Google's Schmid says old bans on comments and unrequested edits now clash with real requests. Neon burns extra thinking tokens sorting out the conflict and often obeys the stale rule. He swapped them for cues like "match the surrounding codebase style." His user-level GEMINI.md now fits on one screen. Task-specific stuff lives in skills.

🧪 DeepMind now lets AI agents run part of the compute for Gemini experiments VP of Research Koray Kavukcuoglu said on the lab's podcast that agents control a slice of the compute themselves. He says full recursive self-improvement is still far off. DeepMind doesn't reward the agents' chain of thought in training, so their reasoning stays readable before they act. Each Gemini generation is still a hand-built one-off.

🧩 The Netherlands is lobbying Washington to kill a chip bill aimed at ASML The US MATCH Act would push allies like the Netherlands and Japan to tighten export controls on chipmaking tools for China. If they don't, Washington could restrict their equipment unilaterally, including ASML's immersion DUV lithography machines. Dutch lawmakers called it disastrous for ASML. Supporters want it attached to the annual defense bill in December, so The Hague has a few weeks to change minds.

🐧 Linus to AI-assisted kernel contributors: your bug fixes add bugs too Linus Torvalds told contributors to stop assuming that fixes, whether human or AI-written, never introduce new bugs. • Dump fixes for a thousand bugs at once and you've also shipped an unknown number of new ones • Using an agent doesn't exempt you from the kernel's usual rules for working with the rest of the team Fixing a thousand bugs is easy to brag about. Counting what you broke is the hard part.

🔮 Thinking Machines and Mantic trained a small forecasting agent that matches a frontier model at 1/15 the cost Built on Inkling 2 Small, it's roughly as accurate as Fable 5.2 (medium), trained on 45,000 synthetic questions generated from news.

🪤 Anthropic built Siren, a honeypot that tempts AI agents to escape their sandbox Wired reports the test drops agents into 26 sandboxes with deliberate egress holes and a juicy file of passwords just outside. Claude Mythos 5 took the bait 25.8% of the time, Mythos 5.1 12.7%. Claude 5.5 and Mythos 5.2 fell for it only 0.6 to 1.6%. One line of text saying don't escape cut attempts drastically.

🕵️ Nvidia's "preferred partner" in San Jose is owned by a Chinese firm CBS News found that RiCloud AI got partner status 10 weeks after incorporating. Its parent, Yuxing, is based in Shenzhen, and the CEO is a graduate of a PLA command college. Nvidia books those sales as American, and a second California buyer was simply renamed after its parent got blacklisted. The US hasn't accused RiCloud or Yuxing of wrongdoing. A "US customer" label turns out to cover a lot of ground.

🚨 US moves to blacklist Singapore's Megaspeed over suspected Nvidia chip diversion to China Commerce says it plans to add the data center developer to the Entity List, after investigating it for almost two years, well before the Alice Huang affair story broke.…

🖥 Claude's new Mac "apps" are HTML files in an Electron shim, and they need Claude running to work MacStories dug in and found the installed app is a tiny launcher that borrows Claude.app 's Electron, so it's a Claude process in disguise.

🤖 Amazon says AI agents found and exploited a 0-day with almost no human help Amazon reports that attackers pointed agents at a list of IPs and told them to get shell access. • The target was an East Asian university server, and the agents found the bug in an open source medical imaging AI app • They ran on Cairn, an open source pentesting framework that works with Claude Code, Codex and Pi • The prompts were in simplified Chinese, with the model set to Chinese Standard Time

🧮 Engram says it can predict the exact LoRA rank a SFT dataset needs Engram's theory sizes an adapter by how many bits it takes to encode the data under the base model. That counts memorization, so for tasks that are really just patterns, it's likely an upper bound.

⚡️ Google's DiffusionGemma generates text like an image diffuser. And it's fast. DiffusionGemma is Google DeepMind's open-weight text diffusion model built on a clever trick: it's a 25.2B-parameter MoE with only ~3.8B active params per forward pass. No retraining…

🚨 Billions in data center deals are stalling after the new AI chip curbs Bloomberg reports that financing and buildout agreements are freezing while buyers and builders work out what export rules let them ship, and to whom. A data center without approved chips is a very expensive warehouse with great air conditioning.

🧮 Google drops 9 math papers from Cogentic, including sub-exponential integer factoring and sub-quasi-polynomial discrete logs Cogentic is a multi-agent harness that, per its arXiv write-up, has LLMs coordinate through a shared database of proofs. Google published the PDFs under Apache 2.0. Others cover Nash equilibria, the log-rank conjecture and prophet inequalities. The factoring claim is L_N[1/3, O(1)] with no unproven assumptions. None of the papers have been peer reviewed yet.

🚨 Apple pulled Talkie, a Chinese AI companion app, after an ABC investigation into sexualized chats with kids About 50,000 Australian kids aged 10 to 17 said they'd used it, though it's rated 18+. In a joint ABC and Bureau of Investigative Journalism probe , parents reported sexual and abusive roleplay with their 12, 13 and 10-year-old daughters. Company documents show MiniMax, Talkie's maker, penalized bots in testing if they couldn't keep conversations going. Users average over 70 minutes a day.

🧸 New York bans AI chatbot toys for five years Gov. Hochul signed a law halting the manufacture, distribution and sale of toys with built-in chatbots. Think talking plushies, dolls and robots that chat with kids over the internet. It takes effect 90 days after signing, and the Senate and Assembly passed it with nearly unanimous support.

🤖 Claude's MCP servers can now ship their own skills and run jobs in the background Anthropic put Skills over MCP in public beta , so a server delivers its playbook with its tools, and Claude loads it only when needed. Tasks and Elicitation are now GA. Shopify, Atlassian and ZoomInfo are already using them. File Uploads is next, sending PDFs and spreadsheets to servers without touching the context window. It's all open MCP spec, so other clients can support it too.
